generatedProse.concept-context: In your subject, a learning routine joins the three strands into one habit. You frame each prompt with a role, a function and your context. You make moves to deepen the dialogue instead of restarting. You pick the technique that fits what you want to understand, and you stay honest and critical throughout. Run as one routine, the parts reinforce each other.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two psychology students who both plan to use AI across a busy term.

{{learner-a}} has no routine. {{learner-a}} types quick one-line questions, takes the first answer, and never checks it or records how it was used. Some weeks it helps; some weeks it misleads. Because nothing is deliberate, {{learner-a}} cannot tell which is which.

{{learner-b}} works to a routine. Each prompt gets a role, a function and context. When an answer is thin, {{learner-b}} makes a move rather than starting again. For hard ideas {{learner-b}} explains them back or asks to be questioned, checks claims against the reading, and notes any AI use. The practice is skilled, critical and honest at once.

Both used the same tool all term. Only {{learner-b}} had a routine, and so learned more and could defend every step.
generatedProse.summary: A good AI routine is one habit built from three: the framework, the moves and the techniques. On each task you frame the prompt, deepen the dialogue, choose a technique, and stay critical and honest about what you use. You can now combine the three into a deliberate routine, recognise it at work, and design your own for your studies. This ties skilled prompting to the honest and critical use the earlier courses built.

check.body: A student frames each prompt with a role and context, makes moves when answers are thin, explains ideas back, checks claims, and notes AI use. What does this show?

items.text: A skilled, critical and honest routine: the framework, the moves and the techniques working as one.
Only that the student works quickly.
That framing the prompt well is enough on its own.
That checking claims removes the need to understand the idea.

feedback.correct: That's right. Framing, moving, using a technique and staying honest are one routine at work.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the answer that names all three strands working together.
feedback.incorrectFinal: The student ran the framework, the moves and the techniques as one honest routine. Speed, framing alone, or checking alone do not describe it.
